|firstmade=[[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]<ref name="2 BBY">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the zero point in the [[Galactic Standard Calendar]], to 35:3 under the [[Great ReSynchronization]] dating system. ''The Essential Atlas'' also places the [[Battle of Selaggis]] on 43:2:28 and the [[Battle of Dathomir (Hunt for Zsinj)|Battle of Dathomir]] on 43:3:21. ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' and ''The Essential Atlas'' both place the Battle of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]]. ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' also places the Battle of [[Selaggis system/Legends|Selaggis]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], confirming the placement of the division between each Galactic Standard Calendar [[Standard year/Legends|year]] as the third [[Standard month/Legends|month]] in the Great ReSynchronization year. Thus, there is a two-month gap between the two dating systems, and the first two months of a GrS year are the last two of the preceding Galactic Standard Calendar year. According to {{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|life/13228_2.html|RM&S; Debates Calendar Reform}}, the Great ReSynchronization was instituted 13 years prior to the article's publication on 13:2:28. Using this information and the Battle of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin's]] GRS date allow us to determine that the Great ReSynchronization was instituted in [[35 BBY/Legends|35 BBY]] and date the afformentioned article to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. Thus, there is a total difference of 35 years and 2 months between the two systems.<br />Based on the provided information, 33:4:3:08 occurred in the year [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]. According to ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', the [[NR-5 Series Repair Droid]] was produced by [[Kalibac Industries]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], whose beginning is dated to 2 BBY by ''The Essential Atlas''. In addition, according to ''[[Cynabar's Fantastic Technology: Droids]]'', [[Tredwall]] marketed NR knockoffs in 33:4:3:08 (2 BBY), when genuine NR-5s were available for purchase. As a result, it can be assumed that the NR knockoff was introduced in 2 BBY.</ref>

{{Quote|Be careful when purchasing an NR-5. A small company called "Tredwall" is marketing an NR knockoff that works for about ten hours before completely frying all of its circuits!|Kraemr, on Cynabar's Droid Datalog|<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" />}}
The '''NR knockoff''' was a cheap, faulty imitation of [[Kalibac Industries]]'<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> [[Class five droid/Legends|class 5]] [[NR-5 Series Repair Droid]]<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> produced and marketed by "[[Tredwall]]," a small company<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> of [[Outlaw tech/Legends|outlaw techs]] in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|195|Kalibac Industries}}</ref> in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].<ref name="2 BBY" /> It worked for nearly ten [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] before completely frying all of its circuits. An individual known as [[Kraemr]] warned potential NR-5 buyers about Tredwall's NR knockoff on [[Cynabar's Droid Datalog]].<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" />

==Behind the scenes==
The NR knockoff was first mentioned in ''[[Cynabar's Fantastic Technology: Droids]]'', a supplement written by [[Drew Campbell]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' that was released in [[1997]].<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" />
